title: 3.8.22 Lab: Saving-and-Loading Capstone
description: Combine the whole module: save a state object by key, load it back with the missing-key and bad-parse guards, and print the restored values. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Define defaults and a state object
steps.instructions: Create a defaults object with at least two properties, then a state object describing a player with a score and a level.

steps.title: Write a save function
steps.instructions: Define a function called saveState that takes a state object and stores it under a key with localStorage.setItem, converting it with JSON.stringify first.

steps.title: Write a load function with all three questions
steps.instructions: Define a function called loadState that reads the same key. If nothing is stored, return the defaults. Otherwise parse the text inside a try block, and return the defaults from the catch block if the text will not parse.

steps.title: Round-trip it and print the result
steps.instructions: Call save with your state, then call load and use console.log to print a property of the restored object. Check that the value you print is the one you saved.

requirements.title: Save function stores by key
requirements.hint: saveState should call localStorage.setItem with a key and the text.

requirements.title: State converted with stringify
requirements.description: Calls JSON.stringify. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: Turn the state into text with JSON.stringify before you store it.

requirements.title: Load reads the key
requirements.hint: loadState should read the same key with localStorage.getItem.

requirements.title: Missing key handled
requirements.description: Tests the read value against null. Help: 3.8.15 (Saving by Key)
requirements.hint: If the text read back is null, return the defaults right away, before any parsing.

requirements.title: Parse guarded
requirements.description: Wraps JSON.parse in try and catch. Help: 2.5.4 (try...catch: Attempt and Recover)
requirements.hint: Put JSON.parse inside try, and return the defaults from catch.

requirements.title: Restored state logged
requirements.hint: Call saveState, then loadState, and print one property of what loadState returns.

requirements.title: saveState and loadState round-trip a state, and a missing key gives an object
requirements.description: After saveState({ score: 7, level: 2 }), loadState() returns { score: 7, level: 2 }; saving a second state replaces it; with nothing stored loadState() returns an object. Help: 3.8.16 (Example: The Whole Pattern)
requirements.hint: saveState stores JSON.stringify(state) under a key; loadState reads the same key, returns the defaults when it is null, and otherwise returns JSON.parse of the text.

checks.expr: typeof saveState === 'function' && typeof loadState === 'function' && (() => { saveState({ score: 7, level: 2 }); const a = loadState(); saveState({ score: 9, level: 5 }); const b = loadState(); localStorage.clear(); const d = loadState(); return JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify({ score: 7, level: 2 }) && JSON.stringify(b) === JSON.stringify({ score: 9, level: 5 }) && d !== null && typeof d === 'object'; })()
checks.fail: saveState({ score: 7, level: 2 }) then loadState() should give back { score: 7, level: 2 }, a second save should replace it, and loadState() with nothing stored should return your defaults object.
